title: Review and merge gates through fleet: agent review with the deletion-safety second review, merge gate, security scans, branch protection
body:
Part of #2 · key `P2-09`

**Context**
#12 sets up the repository on fleet's shared tools, vendored `.claude/` files and `AGENTS.md` blocks. This issue wires the parts that hold secrets, read untrusted pull request content or decide merges, so it runs on Fable and stays small: callers of fleet's reusable `agent-review.yml` (first review by Sonnet; second review by Fable for risky PRs), `merge-gate.yml`, `security.yml`, `review-mining.yml`, `fleet-sync.yml` and `cancel-on-close.yml`, plus the ruleset on `main`. It merges before wave 2 (`docs/HANDOFF.md`), so every PR after it is reviewed. Darkroom's deletion-safety issues (#24, #27, #37, #38, all labelled `safety-critical`) get the second review automatically.

Darkroom is private on a personal account: code scanning (SARIF upload) and CodeQL aren't available, so the scans fail the workflow on findings instead, and the merge gate can't require CodeQL. #12's `security.yml` bullet planned CodeQL; it is dropped here.

This PR adds `.github/workflows/agent-review.yml`, but `pull_request_target` runs main's copy, so its own review can't run; the owner reviews it by hand.

**Scope**
- `.github/workflows/agent-review.yml` (caller): `pull_request_target` on `main` with `[opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review, labeled, unlabeled]`; `permissions: {}` at the top; `uses: AnthonyPluth/fleet/.github/workflows/agent-review.yml@<sha> # v1.x.y`; secrets `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` by name; `generated`: `docs/openapi.json`, `frontend/src/lib/api-types.ts`, `docs/feature-map.json`; `second-review-labels` default (`safety-critical`, `security`); `second-review-paths`:
  `darkroom/domain/dedupe.py`, `darkroom/domain/eligibility.py`, `darkroom/domain/review.py`, `darkroom/domain/ingest/cleanup.py`, `darkroom/domain/ingest/place.py`, `darkroom/domain/xmp.py`, `darkroom/providers/exiftool.py`, `darkroom/storage/paths.py`, `darkroom/storage/secretbox.py`, `darkroom/oidc.py`, `darkroom/tls.py`, `darkroom/server/handler.py`, `darkroom/server/routes.py`, `darkroom/server/api/cleanup.py`, `darkroom/server/api/review.py`, `darkroom/server/api/uploads.py`, `darkroom/server/api/devices.py`, `darkroom/server/api/browser_internal.py`, `darkroom/server/mcp_*.py`, `darkroom_browser/live.py`, `darkroom_browser/runner.py`, `ios/Packages/DarkroomCore/Sources/**/Cleanup*`, `ios/Darkroom/**/Cleanup*`, `ios/Darkroom/Keychain.swift`, `.semgrep/**`, `SECURITY.md`, `Dockerfile*`, `docker-compose.yml` (`.github/**` and `.claude/**` are built in).
- `.github/agent-review/context.md`: what Darkroom is; private data here is people's names, email addresses, Google account ids, device names, archive ids, photo paths, GPS coordinates and capture times of real photos; fixtures are synthetic (`tests/takeout_fixtures.py`, `tests/fixtures/media.py`); the repository is private but the rule is the same as in Waypoint and Runway.
- `.github/agent-review/invariants.md`: AGENTS.md's promises 1–6 as numbered items, then a section per safety-critical issue that each fills in its PR, append-only: dedupe invariants 1–6 (#24), eligibility invariants 1–7 (#37), `CleanupFlow` rules (#38), review actions never set `confirmed_in_google` (#27); each item names its test or Semgrep rule.
- `.github/workflows/merge-gate.yml` (caller): `workflow_run` of `CI`, `Docker image`, `Security scans`; `check_suite`; `workflow_dispatch` with `pr`; `required-workflows`: `CI`, `Security scans` (no CodeQL); `required-statuses`: `Agent review`, `Second review`. #33 adds `iOS` to both lists when its workflow exists.
- `.github/workflows/security.yml` (caller): `code-paths` `^(darkroom|darkroom_browser|frontend/src|\.semgrep)/`, `web-dirs` `frontend`, `image-paths` `^(Dockerfile|Dockerfile\.browser|\.dockerignore|pyproject\.toml|poetry\.lock)$`, `sarif-upload: false`, `scorecard: false`, weekly cron.
- `.github/workflows/review-mining.yml` (monthly), `fleet-sync.yml` (push to `main` on `.github/workflows/**`, weekly, by hand; `FLEET_BOT_APP_ID` variable and `FLEET_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY` secret by name), `cancel-on-close.yml`. No `deep-scan-due`: Darkroom's deep scans are on demand ({{P2-12}}, {{P6-03}}).
- `.github/CODEOWNERS`: `/.github/`, `/.claude/`, `/AGENTS.md`, `/CLAUDE.md`, `/SECURITY.md`, `/.semgrep/`, `/docs/design/` → `@AnthonyPluth`.
- `docs/runbook.md` "Branch protection" section: the ruleset below and why only "Merge gate" is required.
- Owner steps (checklist in the PR): ruleset on `main` (pull request required, Code Owner review, required status `Merge gate` only, no force push or deletion); secrets `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; `fleet-bot` installed with its variable and secret; labels `security`, `fleet`, `review-mining`. Suggested, not required: add `security` to #14, #28, #32 and #41 (their modules are on the path list anyway).

**Out of scope**
Tools, `.claude/` files and `AGENTS.md` (#12); the `iOS` workflow (#33); deep scans ({{P2-12}}, {{P6-03}}).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Every fleet reference SHA-pinned with a `# v1.x.y` comment, all at the version in `.fleet/version`; `make fleet-checks` and zizmor pass.
- [ ] After merge, a throwaway agent PR touching `darkroom/domain/eligibility.py` gets "Agent review", "Second review" (risky by path) and "Merge gate"; a throwaway PR labelled `safety-critical` with an unrelated change gets "Second review" from the label. Links pasted here; the owner closes them.
- [ ] A planted Semgrep finding on a throwaway branch fails `Security scans` (no SARIF upload needed).
- [ ] The ruleset is in place (owner ticks) and a push straight to `main` is refused.

**Tests**
`make fleet-checks`, `zizmor .github/workflows`, the throwaway PRs.

**Depends on**
#12; `AnthonyPluth/fleet` v1.0.0 (fleet issue `FLEET-RELEASE`); `FLEET-SETUP` done (App installed).

**Model**
Fable (`claude-fable-5-1`): review workflows, CI secrets, untrusted pull request content and security scanning.

title: Demo dataset and demo server: made-up people, accounts, Pixels, devices and originals on a frozen clock
body:
Part of #2 · key `P2-10`

**Context**
Agents should run Darkroom instead of trusting tests, on data that is obviously made up and needs no Google account, iPhone or Immich. Waypoint (`waypoint/verify.py`, `waypoint/domain/demo.py`) and Runway (`runway/verify.py`, `runway/domain/demo.py`) do this with a demo seed, a demo server under libfaketime with a fixed clock, an environment allowlist and a dead outbound proxy; Darkroom follows Waypoint's version. This issue is the data and the server; the browser driver is {{P2-11}}, the fake Immich {{P3-09}}, the import journey {{P3-10}}.

**Scope**
- `darkroom/domain/demo.py`: `seed(conn, photos_root, today)` creating three made-up people (names and `@example.com` addresses that read as fake), two Google accounts (one served by a shared Pixel serving two people, one single), Pixels, one iPhone per person with check-ins relative to `today`, events and one open sign-in alert, and each person's `originals/` filled from `tests/fixtures/media.py`'s synthetic images and videos (with and without GPS, one Live Photo pair), indexed through #19's indexer so Status shows real counts.
- `darkroom/verify.py` (as `waypoint/verify.py`): `FROZEN_NOW` (a fixed noon UTC date), `clean_env` (an allowlist of variables; `HTTP(S)_PROXY` set to `http://127.0.0.1:9`; `NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost`; no OIDC, Home Assistant or Immich credentials; `DARKROOM_DEMO=1`), `seed` and `serve` subcommands under libfaketime, each on its own temporary data directory and photos root.
- Sign-in on the demo server: `verify.py seed` mints a session for a made-up member of the `parents` group, accepted only when the server runs with `DARKROOM_DEMO=1` and listens on 127.0.0.1; the normal configuration refuses it. Tests prove both, and the every-route guard from #14 still holds for every other kind.
- `run.py demo [--data DIR]` seeds a local data directory for a person to look at.
- Home Assistant alerts in demo mode go to a recorder, never a network call.

**Out of scope**
The browser driver and skill ({{P2-11}}), the fake Immich ({{P3-09}}), imports ({{P3-10}}).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `run.py demo` on an empty directory seeds everything above; `GET /api/status` on the demo server shows the three people with non-zero indexed counts.
- [ ] Nothing in the seed reads as a real person, address, place or device (reviewed in the PR; names and coordinates are invented).
- [ ] The demo session is refused without `DARKROOM_DEMO=1`, on a non-loopback bind, and by a production config (tests); `tests/test_every_route.py` still passes.
- [ ] Two seeds at the same `FROZEN_NOW` produce byte-identical databases apart from ids (test).

**Tests**
`tests/test_demo.py`, `tests/test_verify_env.py`, `tests/test_demo_session.py`.

**Depends on**
#13, #14, #18, #19, {{P2-09}}.

**Model**
Fable (`claude-fable-5-1`): it adds a demo-only sign-in path beside #14's guard.

title: tools/control, make verify and the verify-darkroom skill on demo data
body:
Part of #2 · key `P2-11`

**Context**
Waypoint and Runway give agents `tools/control` (a browser session on the demo server, driven one command at a time), `make verify` (every page at phone and desktop width under a frozen clock, plus an accessibility audit) and a `verify-*` skill saying when and how to use them (`.claude/skills/verify-waypoint/`). Darkroom adapts Waypoint's version (`frontend/verify/`), on {{P2-10}}'s demo server. The driver differs too much between the two apps to come from fleet; fleet's `checks` and `verify.yml` cover the parts that are shared.

**Scope**
- `frontend/verify/`: `verify.mjs` (pages at 440×956 and 1280×800, browser clock fixed at `FROZEN_NOW`, every request to anything but the session's server blocked before it is sent, settle rules as Waypoint's), `a11y.mjs` (axe WCAG 2.2 AA, 44 px tap targets at phone width, a visible focus ring), `control.mjs` + `control-daemon.mjs` (doctor, start, stop, cleanup, reset, goto, snapshot, click, type, press, viewport, screenshot, console, network, eval (read-only unless `--write`), flow), `control-smoke.mjs`, `flows/` with a README; `tools/control` shim.
- Pages now: sign-in, Status, People (#17). Each later page issue adds its page to `PAGES` ({{P3-10}} adds Imports and Review).
- `make verify` writes `docs/screenshots/<page>-<width>.png` (committed visual baselines, synthetic data only) and its report to `artifacts/verify/` (ignored); `make verify-skill`, `make user-feature-map`, `make control-smoke`. `[tool.fleet.screenshots]` in `pyproject.toml` points fleet's image check at `docs/screenshots/`. CI: a `control-smoke.yml` caller of fleet's `verify.yml` on changes to `frontend/verify/**`, `darkroom/verify.py`, `tools/control`, and `Control smoke` added to the merge gate's `workflow_run` list (not required).
- `.claude/skills/verify-darkroom/SKILL.md` and `references/` (`cli.md` and `feature-map.md` generated; `gotchas.md`, `journeys.md`, `feature-gotchas.md` written), adapted from verify-waypoint: demo data only, loopback only, no real Google, iPhone or Immich, everything under `artifacts/control/`; screenshots for a UI PR come from `make verify`, never `artifacts/control/`.
- `.claude/hooks/session-start.local.sh` (sourced by fleet's hook): `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` when missing; `libfaketime` through `fleet.conf`'s `APT_PACKAGES`.
- The images are compared by the owner with `docs/design/web/` (#16); this issue changes no UI.

**Out of scope**
Imports and Review pages ({{P3-10}}); any change to a page's look.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] In a fresh cloud session: `tools/control doctor`, `start`, `goto status`, `screenshot` at phone and desktop, `stop` (output pasted).
- [ ] `make verify` writes the sign-in, Status and People images with no console error or 5xx, and the accessibility audit passes; two runs give identical images.
- [ ] A test proves a page's request to any other host is blocked and reported.
- [ ] `make fleet-checks` passes (skill well formed, generated references current, images only in `docs/screenshots/` and the other homes).

**Tests**
`frontend/verify/*.test.mjs` (as Waypoint's), `make control-smoke`, `make verify`.

**Depends on**
#15, #17, #16 (signed-off web design), {{P2-10}}.

**Model**
Opus: a test harness adapted from Waypoint's; no secrets.

title: Fake Immich: a loopback server that serves libraries and records rescans
body:
Part of #3 · key `P3-09`

**Context**
#26 calls Immich through `darkroom/providers/immich.py` (`ping`, `list_libraries`, `find_library`, `rescan_library` with the admin key in `x-api-key`) and its acceptance test expects "the Immich fake" to receive one scan per affected library. One fake serves #26's tests, the demo server ({{P3-10}}) and `tools/control`, so it is its own issue and lands before #26.

**Scope**
- `tests/fakes/immich.py`: `FakeImmich`, a threaded stdlib `http.server` bound to 127.0.0.1 on a free port, serving `GET /api/server/ping`, `GET /api/server/about`, `GET /api/users/me`, `GET /api/libraries` (one per configured person: `id`, `ownerId`, `importPaths`, `exclusionPatterns`), `POST /api/libraries/{id}/scan` (recorded: library id, time, which key); keys checked per request (admin key for scans, per-person keys for reads; 401 otherwise); modes `ok`, `down`, `slow`, `401`, `500` set in code (`fake.mode(...)`) or by `POST /__fake/mode`; `fake.scans()` returns what was recorded.
- `python -m tests.fakes.immich --port N --state FILE` runs it standalone from a JSON state (people, library ids, keys) that {{P2-10}}'s seed writes.
- Field names follow #21's results in `docs/spikes/` when present, else Immich's API reference at the version the spec names; `docs/fakes.md` lists what it covers and what it doesn't.

**Out of scope**
The provider itself (#26); anything Waypoint's photos epic needs from Immich (search, thumbnails).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A test per endpoint and per mode; a wrong or missing key gets 401; scans are recorded in order.
- [ ] It refuses to bind anything but 127.0.0.1 (test).
- [ ] The standalone command serves the state file's libraries.

**Tests**
`tests/test_fake_immich.py`.

**Depends on**
#12.

**Model**
Opus: a test fake; no secrets.

title: Demo import journey: import a fixture export against the fake Immich, then screenshot Imports and the review queue
body:
Part of #3 · key `P3-10`

**Context**
With #22's `TakeoutBuilder`, #26's orchestrator, #27's Imports and Review pages, {{P2-11}}'s driver and {{P3-09}}'s fake Immich, an agent can run the whole ingest on made-up data and look at the result, with no real Google, iPhone or Immich.

**Scope**
- `darkroom/domain/demo.py`: `seed_import(conn, photos_root, today)` builds a `TakeoutBuilder` export seeded against {{P2-10}}'s phone index so it yields every tier (exact, same shot, an `-edited` copy, likely re-encodes that go to review, Google-only items), a Live Photo pair, items without GPS and a sidecar split across parts, then runs `run.py import-takeout --person <demo person> --dir <export>` against the fake Immich.
- `darkroom/verify.py`: starts `FakeImmich` beside each demo server (`IMMICH_URL` and keys from the fake's state); `seed --with-import` runs `seed_import` after `seed`.
- `tools/control start --with-import` and `tools/control fake-immich scans` (prints the recorded rescans).
- `make verify`: pages `imports` and `review` added to `PAGES`; a flow `review-item` that opens one side-by-side item; images at phone and desktop.
- `verify-darkroom` `references/journeys.md`: "Import a fixture export and look at the result" with the commands above.

**Out of scope**
Any change to the Imports or Review pages; a mismatch with #16's signed-off designs is reported in the PR for the owner, not fixed here.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] After `tools/control start --with-import`: the Imports page shows the run with counts equal to the builder's manifest (asserted in Python through `GET /api/imports/{id}`), the fake recorded one rescan per affected library, and the review queue lists the expected likely re-encodes (output and screenshots pasted).
- [ ] `make verify` writes `imports`, `review` and `review-item` images at both widths with no console error or 5xx; two runs give identical images.
- [ ] No request leaves 127.0.0.1 (the control session's network log is clean).

**Tests**
`tests/test_demo_import.py`, the flow, `make verify`.

**Depends on**
#22, #26, #27, {{P2-11}}, {{P3-09}}.

**Model**
Opus: demo data and a verify journey; no secrets.

title: Owner runbook: deep security scan before the first deploy
body:
Part of #2 · key `P2-12`

**Context**
The first deploy to Unraid (after #17, per `docs/HANDOFF.md`, "seed people, accounts and Pixels once P2-05 (#17) is deployed") is the first time Darkroom holds real names, accounts and devices. A deep scan with the claude-security plugin runs before it. The plugin can't run in a workflow (it asks a cost confirmation only the owner's own request can answer and needs a live session; fleet's `docs/deep-scan.md`), so this is an owner runbook.

**Scope**
- At the commit about to be deployed: a local Claude Code session in a fresh clone, `/model claude-fable-5-1`, plugin `claude-security@claude-plugins-official` at user scope, then "scan the whole repository at high effort" with your own sentence accepting the time and token cost (fleet's `docs/deep-scan.md`).
- Findings: Darkroom is private, so one issue per confirmed finding, labelled `security`, with the finding's id and severity; fixes are PRs labelled `security` (they get the second review).
- HIGH and CRITICAL findings block the deploy until fixed and re-checked with a "scan changes" run on the fix.
- Record here: the revision stamp's file name, the effort, counts by severity.
- Optional: a "scan changes" run over the browser worker (#28–#31) before the wave-9 deploy connects Google accounts.

**Out of scope**
Fixing findings (their own issues).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Scan done at the deployed commit; stamp, effort and counts recorded here.
- [ ] No open HIGH or CRITICAL finding when the containers go on Unraid.
- [ ] The report directory was not committed.

**Tests**
None (runbook).

**Depends on**
#14, #17, #18, {{P2-09}}.

**Model**
Owner (no coding model); the scan runs on Fable 5.1.

title: Owner runbook: deep security scan before iPhone cleanup is turned on
body:
Part of #6 · key `P6-03`

**Context**
Deleting from an iPhone is the only step that can lose a photo (`docs/SPEC.md#risks-and-mitigations`). Before the owner enables cleanup on any device (`docs/HANDOFF.md`, after wave 12), a second deep scan looks at the whole repository with the deletion path in focus: dedupe (#24) → review actions (#27) → eligibility and the cleanup API (#37) → the app's `CleanupFlow` (#38).

**Scope**
- As {{P2-12}}: local session, Fable 5.1, whole repository at high effort, plus a scoped scan of `darkroom/domain/dedupe.py`, `darkroom/domain/eligibility.py`, `darkroom/domain/review.py`, `darkroom/server/api/cleanup.py`, `darkroom/server/api/review.py`, `darkroom/server/api/devices.py`, `ios/Packages/DarkroomCore/` and `ios/Darkroom/`.
- Any finding of MEDIUM or above on that path blocks enabling cleanup until fixed.
- Check that the Second review comments on the PRs for #24, #27, #37 and #38 have no blocking finding left unanswered.
- Record here: stamps, efforts, counts by severity.

**Out of scope**
Enabling cleanup itself (owner step after this issue closes).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Both scans recorded; no open finding of MEDIUM or above on the deletion path.
- [ ] The four PRs' Second review threads checked (links here).
- [ ] The report directories were not committed.

**Tests**
None (runbook).

**Depends on**
#37, #38, {{P2-12}}.

**Model**
Owner (no coding model); the scans run on Fable 5.1.
